title: Western Plaguelands
body: The Western Plaguelands were the heart of northern Lordaeron, a country of farms and forests governed from Hearthglen, with Andorhal as the granary of the north. That bounty undid it. The Cult of the Damned tainted the grain, the plague killed the people and raised them as Scourge, and great cauldrons still poison the fields. Now a lich rules Andorhal, Scholomance festers beneath Caer Darrow and the Scarlet Crusade holds Hearthglen, while the Alliance at Chillwind Camp and the Forsaken at the Bulwark hold on at the edges.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Western_Plaguelands (pre-Cataclysm: Hearthglen seat, Andorhal grain hub, cult tainted grain, four cauldrons on largest farmsteads, tumor-like growths, Scarlet Crusade in Mardenholde)

title: Chillwind Camp
body: Chillwind Camp, on the southern edge of the plague lands below the Alterac Mountains, is the Alliance's foothold in the west. Commander Ashlam Valorfist holds it for Stormwind and plans the push on Andorhal, High Priestess MacDonnell leads the war on the plague cauldrons, and officers of the Argent Dawn sign up anyone willing to fight the dead. The camp also shelters Weldon Barov, a nobleman feuding with his own brother.

title: Sorrow Hill
body: Sorrow Hill is the great cemetery south of Andorhal, where the city buried its dead long before the plague. They do not rest: skeletons and ghouls rise from the graves to guard the road to the city. Atop the hill stands the tomb of Uther the Lightbringer, and among the graves the monument of Captain Joseph Redpath of Darrowshire.

parts.body: The ghost of Marlene Redpath haunts her old house on the hill. When the battle of Darrowshire began she hid her young niece, Pamela, and she has never learned what became of the girl.

title: Uther's Tomb
body: Uther the Lightbringer, first paladin of the Order of the Silver Hand, fell to his own student, Prince Arthas, and the survivors raised his tomb atop Sorrow Hill. Its epitaph says that he lived and died to defend Lordaeron. High Priest Thel'danis keeps watch over it and purges the evil from the scourgestones brought to him.

parts.body: Within sight of the tomb lives Myranda the Hag, a master illusionist banished from Mardenholde Keep for speaking against a verdict of the Silver Hand. She still weaves guises for those she trusts, and not all of them are Alliance.
sources: page_text 292 (gameobject 2082, Uther's epitaph)

parts.body: The verdict she spoke against was the one that banished Tirion Fordring. She had been his most trusted advisor when he was Lord of Mardenholde, and she always knew he would call on her again.
sources: page_text 292 (gameobject 2082, Uther's epitaph)

parts.body: Uther's holy mark was lost when he died, and the Scarlet Crusade keeps it in Hearthglen. A draenei anchorite at Chillwind Camp wants it returned to the tomb; a blood knight at the Bulwark, once Uther's student, wants it for revenge for Quel'Thalas.
sources: page_text 292 (gameobject 2082, Uther's epitaph)

parts.body: Brought to the tomb, the mark called up Uther's own ghost. He blessed those who came to honor him, and to the student who meant to defile his tomb he sent only forgiveness.

title: Caer Darrow
body: Caer Darrow, an old fortress on an island in Darrowmere Lake, was the seat of House Barov. To keep their lands beyond their own lifetimes the Barovs struck a bargain with Kel'Thuzad, and beneath the keep grew Scholomance, a school of necromancy. A sickness born there killed the whole town on the eve of a visit from Uther, and its people linger as ghosts, reliving their last ordinary day.

parts.body: The last Barov heirs are brothers and bitter rivals. Alexi stayed with the family and is now undead, lounging under Horde guard at the Bulwark; Weldon fled and lives under Alliance guard at Chillwind Camp. The deeds to the family fortune lie in Scholomance.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Caer_Darrow (Barov seat, deal with Kel'Thuzad, Scholomance, plague before Uther's visit, no survivors, ghosts reliving last memory, lake lifeless and still)

parts.body: The spirits of Eva and Lucien Sarkhoff, servants of the Barovs, linger on the island. When the family turned, its servants became subjects for the Butcher, Doctor Theolen Krastinov, and the Sarkhoffs died in his hands.

title: Ruins of Andorhal
body: Andorhal was the grain distribution center of northern Lordaeron, which made it the perfect tool for the Cult of the Damned: tainted grain went out from its granaries to the villages of the north, and the city soon fell. Here Prince Arthas cut down Kel'Thuzad. Now a Scourge garrison fills the streets under the lich Araj the Summoner, once master of Scholomance, and in a ruined inn the bronze dragon Chromie works to mend a torn timeline.

parts.body: Araj was brought down at last, though a lich is not so easily ended: from the phylactery left where he fell, a shard was carried home as proof that the lord of Andorhal was overthrown.

title: Felstone Field
body: Felstone Field, northwest of Andorhal, is one of four farms where the Scourge raised a great plague cauldron, guarded here by Cauldron Lord Bilemaw. Upstairs in the farmhouse the ghost of Janice Felstone cowers in a corner, frantic to send off a parcel she packed before the plague came. Nearby the Scarlet Crusade has pitched a camp of its own.

parts.body: The parcel reached her kin at last. It held half of a luck charm, and only when her husband John's half was found on the farm and the charm made whole did Janice's ghost find peace.

title: Dalson's Tears
body: North of Andorhal lies the farm once called Dalson's Orchard. The Scourge raised a plague cauldron in its field under Cauldron Lord Malvinious, and the farm keeps smaller horrors of its own: a diary open in the house, a lone skeleton wandering the grounds, and an outhouse locked from outside, its door splintered by something within that batters to get out.

parts.body: The diary told the family's end. When Harold Dalson turned, his wife locked him in the outhouse and meant to flee, but she never left: the wandering skeleton was hers, the key still on her bones.

title: The Writhing Haunt
body: East of Andorhal, under the city walls, a farm has become the Writhing Haunt, its plague cauldron guarded by Cauldron Lord Razarch. In one of its cottages lies Mulgris Deepriver, a tauren druid who came alone to heal what the Scourge had poisoned. The plague took him too, and blind and dying he asks strangers to give the diseased wolves and grizzlies a merciful death.

parts.body: Sensing his end, Mulgris wrote what he had learned of the plague into a glyphed oaken branch meant for the Cenarion Circle. Then, with the suffering beasts at rest, he lay still on the cottage floor.
sources: quests 5222, 5233 descriptions (almost due east of Andorhal, close to the ruined city walls)

parts.body: The branch reached the Cenarion Circle, and in its glyphs the druids found a great store of lore about the Scourge's plague. They promised that his work would not be wasted.

title: Gahrron's Withering
body: Gahrron's Withering, once Gahrron's Quickening, was the farm of Del Gahrron near the border of the Eastern Plaguelands. Its plague cauldron is the hardest of the four in the west: no ghouls shamble here, only wraiths and wailing spirits around Cauldron Lord Soulwrath. Beside the barn lies a forgotten shield once carried by Joseph Redpath of Darrowshire.

title: Hearthglen
body: Hearthglen was the seat of government for these lands, ruled from Mardenholde Keep above the town, and when the plague first struck it held out against the Scourge. Now it is the Scarlet Crusade's stronghold in the west. Workers rebuild the town under the eyes of paladins and priests, lumberjacks cut timber at the Northridge mill below, taken from the family who ran it before the war, and Highlord Taelan Fordring holds the keep.

title: Highlord Taelan Fordring
body: Taelan Fordring is Highlord of the Scarlet Crusade in Hearthglen and master of Mardenholde Keep. His crusaders attack outsiders on sight, his officers hold the pass below the town, and the Highlord himself waits in the keep for reinforcements from Tyr's Hand.

parts.body: He is the son of Tirion Fordring. After Tirion's exile his mother told him his father was dead. He became a paladin of the Silver Hand, threw down its standard at Northdale when the order broke, and rose in the Crusade.
sources: quest 5781 description (his mother told him Tirion had died)

parts.body: For years, he confessed, he had been the Grand Crusader's puppet. Shown the truth, he left Hearthglen to find his father, and Grand Inquisitor Isillien cut him down on the road.

title: Chromie
body: Chromie is the name the bronze dragon Chronormu takes among mortals, in the form of a small, cheerful gnome. She has made her home in a ruined inn in Andorhal, working from another timeline so as not to disturb this one, for someone, most likely the Scourge, has tampered with the city's past. The old tragedy of Darrowshire has caught her eye as well.
